modified_source_files.change: Restore the real and virtual display pointers to wint_t **, matching the existing allocation/free and literal representation.

Use wint_t elements in display diff/insert/delete/copy/padding, remove display-to-wchar_t pointer casts, replace the display wcslen with a cell-count loop, preserve marker bits in debug output, pad and wrap a double-column literal before storing its marker and filler.
Use wint_t buffers for overwrite/insertwrite and the magic-margin cell; eliminate the cursor-rewrite pointer cast; widen genuine wchar_t visual text element-by-element before overwrite.
Match the private terminal output declarations to const wint_t * cell buffers.

inspected_unchanged_marker_sources.role: MB_FILL_CHAR remains ((wint_t)-1), exactly 0xffffffff on the target.
EL_LITERAL remains ((wint_t)0x80000000); literal_add/get retain wint_t handles.
Literal byte buffers, visible-character width, allocation and index encoding remain intact.

representation_rationale: A display row is a zero-terminated array of terminal-column cells, not a wchar_t string. One visible wide character occupies a character or literal-handle cell plus MB_FILL_CHAR cells. Column counts and pointer differences must count wint_t elements.

The first literal handle is 0x80000000. Narrowing it to wchar_t16 produces zero, falsely terminating the row and losing the literal. Later literal handles lose their tag and can appear as unrelated control characters. Narrowing the filler produces 0xffff, which no longer equals MB_FILL_CHAR.

Leaving allocation at wint_t width but casting its storage to wchar_t * is also invalid: wchar_t operations step through half-cells and see zero high halves as premature terminators. No such pointer casts remain in the patched display paths.

terminal__putc already checks the full-width filler before testing EL_LITERAL, then expands literal byte buffers or encodes a normal character. Keeping both checks and all intervening cells at wint_t width preserves literal/color output and two-column accounting.

Public histedit wchar_t interfaces, input/edit/history buffers, prompt callbacks and their encoding remain unchanged. Normal wchar_t text is widened as scalar values; markers are never narrowed through a wchar_t codec.

The existing allocator/free code already uses wint_t ** and sizeof(**b); it does not need replacement. Reinstating that type in EditLine and its consumers aligns access, allocation, resize, free and scroll operations.

The tightly coupled right-margin literal fix follows re_putc: first pad to the next row, then place the literal handle and all of its filler cells. The old literal path clipped its filler at the margin even though the associated visible character still occupied two terminal columns.

remaining_compile_and_api_concerns: No compiler/build/test execution was authorized. The next native build may expose independent diagnostics after refresh.c; there is no claim of a successful full library or examples build.

The patch changes private screen-buffer function signatures and EditLine internals only. Rebuild affected objects with normal header dependencies; do not mix pre-port objects that used wchar_t cell access. Public histedit.h and wchar_t input ABI are unchanged.
The marker width is native wint_t32, not a substitute header/type, compiler width flag or cast-based diagnostic workaround. The fixture deliberately rejects the wrong data model.

The existing MSYS character conversion routines and UTF-16 supplementary-character behavior are outside this display-cell change. This patch neither disables wide support nor claims to add a new char32_t input API; supplementary-character round trips need their own native evidence.

Inherited literal lifecycle issue to observe separately: re_refresh clears and rebuilds the literal table before comparing old/new cell IDs. A callback changing only ignored bytes can reuse an identical ID for different bytes. This patch preserves that existing policy rather than making an unrelated literal-table lifetime redesign.

The white-box fixture validates emitted bytes and the model but is not a terminal emulator. Parent PTY observation remains necessary for visible cursor/margin behavior and installed shared-library/public API compatibility.
